agent_K_learning_value_assessment.methodology: Each item scored 1–5 on four dimensions. Unprocessed cases have minimal explanations (1–2 line ExplanationCorrect, brief distractor texts). Certified cases (not in this batch) have expanded explanations.

scoring_scale.1: Minimal — single sentence, no concept teaching
scoring_scale.2: Below par — states answer but lacks depth
scoring_scale.3: Adequate — teaches concept at basic level
scoring_scale.4: Good — teaches concept with reasoning and traps
scoring_scale.5: Excellent — mini-lesson with standard references, worked examples, and remediation

cross_case_analysis.pattern_identified: BIMODAL QUALITY — Unprocessed cases have a consistent structural pattern: (a) select-type items have strong distractor explanations (scoring 4 on remediation) while correct-answer explanations remain 1–2 lines; (b) numeric/fill/match items have minimal 1-line explanations with zero teaching content; (c) multi-select items typically only explain the WRONG choice, leaving correct choices with empty ExplanationWrong slots. This is the signature of template-based draft authoring before certification-grade explanation expansion.

combined_findings.F1: BIMODAL EXPLANATION QUALITY — Unprocessed cases consistently have excellent distractor explanations for select-type items (averaging 4/5 on remediation quality) but 1–2 line explanations for everything else. The template is: select items get full distractor text at authoring time, but correct-answer explanations and numeric/fill/match items get only formula substitution. This is the draft-authoring signature, not a defect — these cases were designed for certification-grade expansion.
combined_findings.F2: CERTIFICATION URGENCY — 28 of the 42 evaluated items (67%) have select or multi items with strong exam-prep value (averaging 4.0+/5.0). With certification-grade explanation expansion (following the CBQ-E1/CBQ-F1 template), these 42 items could reach learner-pool eligibility quickly. Domain C is the critical priority — zero Certified case items exist for Performance Management.
combined_findings.F3: DOMAIN D/E/F UNDERREPRESENTATION — scored_cases.js has only 2 cases each for Domains D, E, F vs. 3 each for A, B, C. Three cases (CBQ-D3, CBQ-E3, CBQ-F3) are missing from the expected 18-case design. scored_cases3/4/5 files (in other packs) may provide supplementary coverage. Cross-file blueprint audit recommended.
combined_findings.F4: CROSS-TAGGING VALUE — E2 and F2 carry dual SectionTags [E,F], providing natural IT audit crossover that mirrors the real CMA exam's increasing integration of technology and controls. This is good exam design but requires careful item-level domain attribution.
